title: Introduce windowed burst governor and proactive drain adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a windowed burst governor to enforce per-tenant burst budgets and a proactive drain adapter to avoid long-tail queueing during decommits. Improves utilization telemetry and exposes new metrics for burn-rate and pending-drain_watermark.
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of tail behavior on Dedicated fleets: (1) tenants consuming short, repeated microbursts that bypassed percentile-based guards and (2) long decommit-induced queueing when a pool shrank. This PR introduces a windowed burst governor that enforces a sliding-window budget and a proactive drain adapter that schedules graceful KV-cache/KV-prefix decompression and request redirection before hard drains.

Design summary: The governor maintains per-tenant sliding windows (configurable length and resolution) and charges requests against a burst budget using a token-decay model. Tokens are replenished at a steady rate tied to each tenant's committed throughput; burst spend is capped by a soft and a hard threshold. The proactive drain adapter listens to planned pool decommits and initiates a three-step pre-drain: marker emission, KV-prefix pre-decompression, and progressive routing to warmlets. This reduces cold-eviction amplification and keeps tail latency under SLOs.

- 7e3f2b2: initial governor implementation + sliding window store + token decay math
- b91a5d8: proactive drain adapter and reconcile loop + warmlet routing hook
- c4aa2e1: metrics + prometheus labels + new burn_rate and pending_drain_watermark metrics
- 9d0f4a5: integration test harness for pool decommits and drain sequencing
- f2c1b8a: config knobs, defaults, and feature flag wiring

Changed areas (small illustrative list):
- serving/autoscale/governor/windowed_burst.go -- core token store and accounting algorithms
- serving/autoscale/drain/adapter.go -- proactive drain orchestration and hooks into scheduler
- serving/telemetry/telemetry.go -- new metrics registration and tagging helpers
- infra/config/defaults.yaml -- new governor config block and feature flag
- tests/integration/decommit_pre_drain_test.go -- end-to-end scenario (mock pools)

Observability notes: New metrics added: "redwood.burst.burn_rate_per_tenant" (gauge, tok/s), "redwood.burst.window_utilization" (histogram), "redwood.drain.pending_watermark" (gauge). Exposed labels: tenant_id, pool_id, pool_region, feature_gate. Dashboards updated under "Dedicated / Burst Governance" and an alert rule added: "BurstBudgetExhausted" when >10% tenants hit hard threshold for >30s.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Diego Alvarez: "Token accounting looks reasonable, but can you add a deterministic test for simultaneous multi-tenant spikes? Concerned about races in the store's eviction path."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added deterministic multi-tenant spike test (tests/unit/windowed_burst_multi_test.go) and made the eviction path lock-free using per-shard compare-and-swap; added comment explaining tradeoffs."
- Priya Nair: "We need to ensure labels are stable for long-term cardinality. Recommend collapsing some pool labels and adding an opt-out config."
- Maya Chen: "Collapsed pool_region -> region label and added config.telemetry.reduce_cardinality flag. Documented default behavior in telemetry.go."
- Thomas Becker: "Verified integration test results against simulated decommit schedule; minor nits about log verbosity."
- Thomas Becker: "LGTM after nits addressed."

CI summary:
- build/linux: pass
- unit-tests: pass (1 flaky test rerun succeeded: serving/scheduler/policy_test.go)
- integration: pass (decommit_pre_drain_test scenario exercised)
- perf/bench: warn (initial benchmark showed 3% p95 increase in tight microbench; optimized by reducing mutex hold in token store -> final run within 0.5% baseline)

Risk and rollouts: Feature is behind feature.windowed_burst_governor flag and default-disabled for existing dedicated customers. Config defaults are conservative (short window, low refill rate). We will enable for a small set of internal fleets first and monitor burn_rate and tail-latency dashboards for two weeks before wider rollout.
